row.evidence: Vault's SCIM docs say "Appropriate Vault Enterprise license required" and that Vault Enterprise supports SCIM 2.0 "as a beta feature for provisioning identity users and groups".
row.notes: SCIM 2.0 is a beta feature of self-managed Vault Enterprise 2.x and later (Enterprise license, Contact Sales), turned on with the enable-scim activation flag; HashiCorp discourages beta features in production. SCIM users map to Vault identity entities and groups to internal identity groups; it does not manage policies. active=false disables the entity (its tokens cannot be used but are not revoked). Auth is a Vault token tied to the SCIM client's entity (any auth method; token TTL from the auth mount). SCIM is not documented for HCP Vault Dedicated or Community. No IdP-specific SCIM guide; Okta's OIN app is OIDC sign-in only. The pricing page would not load (Vercel checkpoint; WebFetch returns only the Terraform tab), so no tier prices are recorded; HCP Vault Dedicated is billed per cluster-hour by edition (Starter, Development, Essentials, Standard) plus clients. OIDC/JWT sign-in is in Community; SAML needs Enterprise or HCP Vault Dedicated. The HashiCorp Cloud Platform portal has its own SCIM for HCP organization users (not Vault identities). The identity entity/group API is available without the SCIM gate.

auth.token_source: Vault token minted for the entity set as the SCIM client's access_grant_principal (e.g. token role + entity alias)
auth.token_expiry: Token TTL of the auth mount

deprovision.data_retained: active=false sets the entity to disabled; its tokens cannot be used but are not revoked. DELETE removes the entity.

roles.how: SCIM does not manage Vault policies; groups map to internal identity groups.

limitations.text: Beta feature; HashiCorp strongly discourages beta features in production.
Must be activated with the enable-scim activation flag before use.
User PATCH only supports replacing active; group PATCH only member add/remove; no /Me, bulk, sort, ETag or password change.
externalId is required on create and immutable; nested groups not allowed.
Each SCIM client only sees and manages the users and groups it created.

capabilities.notes: Users are identity entities; deactivate = disabled flag; roles = policies attached to entities/groups.

limitations.text: Entities provisioned through SCIM should be managed through the SCIM endpoints.
